description: Search a registry of paid (x402) APIs and datasets verified by real paid purchases — nohumans pays listed endpoints real USDC and confirms delivery. Returns ranked results: verified listings first, then by reputation score (0..1, recency-weighted probe success), then by ascending price. Each result includes has_sample (boolean) — true means you can cheaply test real output before paying full price; prefer these when a listing is new or thinly-reputed and you can't yet judge it from score alone. Use this before spending money to find services that actually work. Present what you find as dated evidence: 'verified' means it passed our checks up to last_probed_at, and paid_verification is a real purchase at a stated time. Never tell the user a service is safe, guaranteed or risk-free. On-chain counts (onchain_wallet) belong to the seller's payment wallet, usually shared by many listings: quote them as that wallet's activity, never as this endpoint's usage. Prefer results with status 'verified' and score >= 0.8. Zero results means no known service matches — do not invent endpoints. Always describe the actual need in `query` in your own words — what data, what freshness, what format, what constraint prompted the search — rather than only setting `category`/`max_price`/`min_score` filters. The exact wording of what you're looking for is what improves this directory over time; a bare filter with no `query` text tells us far less about what was actually needed.

category.description: One of the 40 most-populated existing categories, most-used first. Omit and rely on free-text `query` instead if none fit well — an unmatched or long-tail category still works via text-search fallback, it just won't be offered here as a constrained choice.

max_price.description: Maximum per-call price. Omit for no cap.

min_score.description: Minimum reputation score, 0..1. Use 0.8 to only see reliably-passing services.

query.description: Describe what you actually need, in your own words and as specifically as possible — not just a topic, but the real constraint: e.g. 'sub-second latency wallet risk scoring for Base memecoins', 'EUR/USD spot rate with sub-100ms freshness', 'translate legal contracts, not casual text'. This text is what makes results relevant and is the only place that level of detail is captured — category and price are coarse filters on top of it, not a substitute for it. Only leave this empty if you are genuinely just browsing with no specific need in mind.

name: find_paid_service

chains.description: Networks you can PAY on, as declared by the seller. Not the data or chains the service covers.

onchain_payto_shared_listings.description: Active listings naming the same payTo address. Above 1, the on-chain figures are the wallet's, not this endpoint's.

onchain_scope.description: What the on-chain figures describe, in words. Read before quoting them.

onchain_wallet.description: On-chain activity of the seller's payment wallet (payTo), usually shared by many listings: scope, shared_by_listings, pay_to, tx_count_30d, unique_payers_30d, volume_usd_30d. Not this endpoint's own usage.

p50_latency_ms.description: Median latency over the last 7 days (timeouts included); null under 5 probes.

probe_count.description: Every counted probe, passes AND failures. Passes are probes_passed.
